name: CIDEC-related Familial Partial Lipodystrophy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for CIDEC-related FPLD

criteria.description: Regional loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue predominantly affecting the limbs and trunk with preservation or accumulation in the face and neck
Presence of insulin resistance, diabetes mellitus, hypertriglyceridemia, or hepatic steatosis
Identification of pathogenic heterozygous mutation in the CIDEC gene
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance of partial lipodystrophy
Exclusion of other causes of lipodystrophy such as HIV-associated or acquired generalized lipodystrophy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of regional partial lipodystrophy, metabolic complications, and a pathogenic CIDEC gene mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for confirmation; clinical presentation may overlap with other lipodystrophy syndromes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue in limbs
Loss of gluteal subcutaneous adipose tissue

laboratory: Elevated fasting insulin and glucose levels indicating insulin resistance
Hypertriglyceridemia with triglyceride levels often >500 mg/dL
imaging: MRI or CT showing selective loss of subcutaneous fat in limbs and trunk
Ultrasound or MRI evidence of hepatic steatosis
other: Skin biopsy showing reduced adipocyte size and number in affected areas

distinguishingFeatures: More generalized fat loss including face
Earlier onset of cardiac conduction defects
More prominent fat loss in limbs and gluteal region
Generalized fat loss including face and trunk

redFlags: Rapid onset of severe insulin resistance in young adult
Severe hypertriglyceridemia refractory to standard treatment
Family history of partial lipodystrophy or metabolic syndrome
references: Garg A. Lipodystrophies. Am J Med. 2000;108(2):143-152.
Kim CA, et al. CIDEC mutation causes familial partial lipodystrophy. J Clin Invest. 2016;126(1):339-345.
Orphanet: CIDEC-related familial partial lipodystrophy. ORPHA:435651.
